Merdeka 118 Tower

The tallest building in Malaysia 2025
ABOUT

The second tallest building in the world

Merdeka 118 — a skyscraper in Kuala Lumpur with a height of 679 meters, built in 2023.

Merdeka 118 has become the second tallest building in the world after Burj Khalifa in Dubai (828 meters). It is also the tallest building in Malaysia and the entire Southeast Asia region.

The building was officially opened by the King of Malaysia on January 10, 2024, but construction work inside is still ongoing. The observation deck are expected to open in Q2-Q3 2025. Park Hyatt hotel hotel is scheduled to open in Q2 2025, and shopping center are expected to open no earlier than Q3 2025.

FAQ

Answers to frequently asked questions about the skyscraper.

The architectural height of the tower, including the spire, is 678.9 meters (2,227 feet). The spire itself measures 158 meters, and the top floor reaches a height of 517.4 meters.

Merdeka 118 has become the tallest building in Malaysia, surpassing the Exchange 106 skyscraper (453 meters).

It has also claimed the top spot among the tallest buildings in Southeast Asia, surpassing Landmark 81 in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (461 meters).

The skyscraper is situated in the center of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

The building consists of 118 floors, which is reflected in its name.

The majority of the floors house office spaces. Additionally, there is a 7-story shopping center called Mall 118, the Park Hyatt Kuala Lumpur hotel, The View At 118 observation deck, and a luxury restaurant located within the building.

The building was officially opened on January 10, 2024. However, construction work inside Merdeka 118 is still ongoing. It is expected that the observation deck and hotel will be opened in the 2nd to 3rd quarter of 2025.

The ticket prices for the skyscraper’s observation decks will be known after the official opening of the tower.

Presumably, the ticket price for Merdeka 118 will be slightly higher than the Petronas Towers ($25) in Kuala Lumpur.

In Malay language, “Merdeka” means “independence.” The tower received its name from the nearby Merdeka Stadium, where in 1957, prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman declared Malaysia’s independence from Britain.

According to reports, approximately 5 billion ringgit (1.07 billion dollars) was spent on the construction of the tower.
